newsitem.title: USA: U.S. July real earnings down 1.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. July real earnings down 1.0 pct.

text.p: U.S. workers' average weekly earnings, after adjusting for inflation and seasonal factors, fell 1.0 percent in July, the Labor Department said on Thursday.
The July decrease followed a revised 0.8 percent gain in June real average weekly earnings. Previously, the department reported that June real earnings rose 0.5 percent.

The July decline reflects a drop of 0.9 percent in average weekly hours along with a 0.2 percent increase in the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers, the Labor Department said.
Real average weekly earnings last month were 1.4 percent lower than the July 1996 level, the department said.
In constant 1982 dollars, weekly earnings for non-supervisory private workers outside the farm sector averaged a seasonally adjusted $258.90 in July, versus $261.64 in June and $254.45 in July 1996.
In current dollars, weekly earnings averaged a seasonally adjusted $420.71 in July, compared with $424.38 in June and $405.08 in July last year, it said.
